clue.text: Court work with little time for good turn amid depression

indicators.note: amid means the other pieces sit in the middle of the depression word

parts.note: a sump is a pit or hollow where liquid collects, a depression
MIN is the short form of minute, a little time
U stands for a turn, as in a U-turn

explanation.surface: Someone gets a short spell of community service for a good deed while feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amid' signals the container. 'Court work' is the judge's closing review of the evidence for a jury, not tennis or work at a royal court.
explanation.definitionFit: In a trial the judge's address reviewing the evidence for the jury is a central piece of courtroom work.

clue.text: Scene of witches at the opening of Macbeth after disposal?

indicators.note: after puts the Macbeth letter behind the disposal word

parts.note: a sale is a disposal of goods

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here of Macbeth

explanation.surface: Asks where Macbeth's witches appear when the play begins, once they have been got rid of.
explanation.walkthrough: Macbeth suggests the play's three witches, but the witches meant are those of the 1692 trials in Massachusetts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Massachusetts town held notorious witch trials in 1692, so it is a famous setting for witches.

clue.text: Heart-warming lots of letters about the aim of changing conditions

indicators.note: about here means concerning: letters on the subject of the aim, so the letters word follows the aim word

parts.note: something heart-warming is touching or moving
taken as written
a goal is an aim
post is mail, lots of letters

explanation.surface: A touching bundle of correspondence on the subject of purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means altering the rules or targets unfairly while something is under way.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes unfairly altering the rules or targets midway, so changing the conditions.

clue.text: Show up friend keeping at home after sick turn

indicators.note: after says the friend part comes behind the sick turn part

parts.note: ill means sick
U stands for a turn, as in a U-turn

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so the friend word holds the at-home word

parts.note: a mate is a friend
in means at home

explanation.surface: A friend who stays home after falling ill turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' signals the container and 'after' the order. 'Show up' looks like expose, but here it means light up.
explanation.definitionFit: To light something up is to show it up clearly, the literal sense of shedding light on it.

clue.text: One with knowledge of sin got punished by church leader

indicators.note: punished suggests the letters are knocked about into a new order
a leader is the first, so the first letter of church

explanation.surface: A sinner who got punished by the head of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punished' is the anagram signal; 'church leader' looks like a bishop but is just the first letter of church.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek root gnosis means knowledge, so a gnostic is one claiming special spiritual insight.

clue.text: Dealing with washing on the 9?

definitions.meaning: fixing laundry to a line with clothes pegs
the first word of 9 across means even; the phrase ... plus that word means neck and neck in a contest

explanation.surface: Hanging out washing on the line referred to in 9.
explanation.walkthrough: The '9' points to the first word of 9 across, and pegging that word is an idiom for keeping pace with a rival.
explanation.definitionFit: Pegging is attaching laundry with clothes pegs, and it also forms the idiom for being level with a rival.

clue.text: High will be low shortly: having high frequency's unknown

parts.note: L is the short form of low
oft means often, at high frequency
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A paradox about high becoming low, with a high frequency whose value is unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like radio jargon, but 'high frequency' is simply often, and 'low shortly' is L, as on a switch.
explanation.definitionFit: Lofty means tall or elevated, a synonym for high.

clue.text: See 20
See 9
Is the song history?

definitions.meaning: something that is history belongs to the past

explanation.surface: Asks whether the song is now a thing of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beatles song is famous enough to be 'the song'; and what is history is over, in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: It names the famous Beatles ballad, and as a noun it means the recent past, which is history.

clue.text: Fair conditions, even with spreading net widely?

parts.note: level means even
... the ... means seeking many partners, casting a wide net

explanation.surface: Asks whether fairness comes with casting a net far and wide.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'playing the field' (dating many people) is used without its 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: An even ground for competition is the standard metaphor for fair conditions for everyone.

clue.text: Started in Scottish (not Northern) isles: they get depressed in church

indicators.note: in tells us the started word goes inside the isles word
not tells us the Northern letter is removed

parts.note: with isles, the Orkneys are a Scottish island group
gan is an archaic word for began or started
the plural S of the island group's name

explanation.surface: A tale about something beginning in the Scottish islands, though not the northern ones, and church-goers getting depressed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Orkneys are islands off Scotland's north coast. Removing N ('not Northern') gives ORKEYS, and GAN ('Started', archaic) goes 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: The keys of a church organ are pressed down by the organist, so they literally get depressed.

clue.text: Araucaria absent in exam about dealing with comparison of pressures

indicators.note: about means around, so the exam word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: matric is short for matriculation, an entrance exam
no means absent, as in no one there
the setter refers to himself, so me

explanation.surface: The setter is missing from an exam on pressure gauges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container. Setters often refer to themselves as me, so 'Araucaria absent' becomes no me; matric is short for matriculation, a school-leaving or entrance exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A manometer is an instrument comparing fluid pressures, and this adjective describes such measurement.

clue.text: Ridley's no use

indicators.note: the 's stands for has: Ridley has these letters within it

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on someone called Ridley.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Ridley's' as 'Ridley has': the letters sit inside the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle can mean futile or pointless, as in idle threats, so of no use.

clue.text: Filler for a garden centre in 1008

indicators.note: to centre in is to place within the middle, so the other pieces go inside the number

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral 1000, followed by eight
Kew Gardens in London is the famous botanic garden

explanation.surface: A garden centre sells something as a filler, all for 1008.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre in' signals the container; 1008 is the Roman numeral for 1000 plus the word eight. Kew is the Royal Botanic Gardens in London. 'Garden centre' looks like one phrase but is split.
explanation.definitionFit: A makeweight is something added just to fill out a deal or make up a weight, a filler.

clue.text: Leather first seen in pouch in these mills

indicators.note: seen in tells us these pieces appear inside the pouch word

parts.note: a sac is a pouch
to tan is to treat hide into leather, or to beat, give a leathering
I is one, the first number

explanation.surface: Leather is noticed for the first time in a pouch made at a mill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'these mills' points to Blake's 'dark Satanic mills' in the hymn Jerusalem; the answer is the word describing them.
explanation.definitionFit: Blake's hymn Jerusalem calls the mills of industrial England dark and diabolical in exactly this word.

clue.text: Capital to keep at home, say

parts.note: to stock is to keep goods in supply

indicators.note: say tells us to take the sound of the word home, not its spelling

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like HOLM

explanation.surface: Advice about having a capital sum to keep at home.
explanation.walkthrough: HOLM (a river island) is pronounced like 'home', which 'say' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the capital city of Sweden.

clue.text: Talked about revolution starting and got arrested?

indicators.note: about means going round, so the talk word goes round the letter

parts.note: to gab is to chat, so gabbed means talked

indicators.note: the starting letter of revolution

explanation.surface: People who chattered about the start of the revolution were taken into custody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R, from 'revolution starting', inside GABBED.
explanation.definitionFit: Grabbed means got hold of, seized, as a suspect is seized when arrested.

clue.text: Former BBC man's change of heart is a demographic concern

parts.note: John Birt was Director-General of the BBC from 1992 to 2000

indicators.note: change of means the letters of the following word are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ex-BBC boss has a change of heart about population figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of' rearranges HEART into HRATE. 'change of heart' looks like the idiom but is an anagram instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: The number of births per head is a basic measure that population studies watch closely.

clue.text: Shopping convenience for the honest operator

indicators.note: the letters are taken for the clue from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Praises a convenient shop as good for an honest trader.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'hONEST OPerator'.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop or centre where all needs are met in one visit is a convenience to shoppers.

clue.text: See 9
They say I wander where the rocks are

indicators.note: they say tells us the letters are those that sound like the spoken words

parts.note: I stray means I wander

explanation.surface: A rambler claims to roam over the rocky landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' means ice cubes, as in a drink 'on the rocks'; the clue sounds like a walk among real rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocks is slang for ice cubes, and a freezer tray is where the cubes are made and kept.

Cast aside excitement involved with the girl astride a horse (said right?)

clue.text: Cathedral has one: it rates the tops

definitions.text: Cathedral has one: it rates the tops

indicators.note: the tops of words are their first letters, taken from the five words before

explanation.surface: A cathedral boasts a singing group it rates as the very best.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the first letters of 'Cathedral has one: it rates'; the whole clue is also the definition, since a cathedral has one.
explanation.definitionFit: Every cathedral has a body of singers leading its services, which this clue presents as top-rated.

clue.text: Man of war to roll about — let this be changed

indicators.note: about means around, so the roll goes round the other letters

parts.note: a bap is a soft bread roll

indicators.note: be changed instructs the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A warship sets out to roll about, with a call for it to be altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be changed' is the anagram signal and 'about' the container. A bap is a soft British bread roll; 'roll' looks like a ship rolling in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-of-war is an old term for an armed warship, and this is the heavily armed kind.

clue.text: See 2
See 2
First in the ENT department? I wish I could see the point

parts.note: O to, as in O to be in England, expresses a wish
lo is an old word for see or behold
the gist is the point of something

explanation.surface: A patient in the ear, nose and throat clinic wishes they understood what the point was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First in the ENT department' is Ear, the E of ENT, so the specialist meant is an ear doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: An otologist specialises in the ear, which is the first part of Ear, Nose and Throat.

clue.text: See 20
Is it mounted twice on the wall?

definitions.text: Is it mounted twice on the wall?

parts.words: Is it mounted twice on the wall?
parts.note: a picture hung on the wall is mounted once; one painted directly on a wall is mounted, and also belongs to the wall, so it is on the wall twice over

explanation.surface: Asks whether a painting has been hung on the wall twice.
explanation.walkthrough: The word itself comes from Latin murus, a wall, so it is on the wall both literally and in its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting applied directly to a wall surface belongs to the wall itself, as its Latin root murus suggests.

clue.text: Achievement of some in the sergeants' mess

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Something to be achieved by certain people in the sergeants' mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' rearranges SERGEANTS. The definition echoes Twelfth Night: 'some achieve greatness'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Twelfth Night says some are born great, some achieve greatness, so greatness is what some achieve.
